topic: Physics: Forces, Thermal, Electromagnetism, Waves & Circuits

questions.question: Two forces of 5 N and 15 N act on an object. Which of the following CANNOT be the magnitude of their resultant force?
questions.explanation: The maximum resultant is 15 + 5 = 20 N (same direction). The minimum is 15 - 5 = 10 N (opposite directions). Any value outside 10 N to 20 N is impossible.

questions.question: Two forces, each of magnitude 10 N, act on an object at an angle of 90° to each other. What is the magnitude of the resultant force?
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras' theorem: Resultant = √(10² + 10²) = √200 ≈ 14.1 N.

questions.question: A car is travelling along a straight horizontal road at a constant velocity of 20 m/s. What is the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the car?
options: Depends on the mass of the car
questions.explanation: According to Newton's First Law, an object moving at constant velocity has zero acceleration, meaning the resultant force acting on it is exactly 0 N.

questions.question: Three forces act on a point object and keep it in equilibrium. If two of the forces are 6 N and 8 N acting at 90° to each other, what is the magnitude of the third force?
questions.explanation: For equilibrium, the third force must exactly balance the resultant of the first two. Resultant of 6 N and 8 N at 90° is √(6² + 8²) = 10 N. The third force is 10 N in the opposite direction.

questions.question: Which statement correctly defines the specific heat capacity of a substance?
options: The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of the substance by 1 °C
The energy required to raise the temperature of the entire object by 1 °C
The energy required to change 1 kg of the substance from solid to liquid at constant temperature
The total internal energy contained within 1 kg of the substance
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity (c) is defined as the thermal energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass (1 kg) of a substance by 1 K (or 1 °C).

questions.question: Block A and Block B are made of the same material. Block A has twice the mass of Block B. How do their heat capacities compare?
options: Block A has half the heat capacity of Block B
Block A has the same heat capacity as Block B
Block A has twice the heat capacity of Block B
Block A has four times the heat capacity of Block B
questions.explanation: Heat capacity (C) = mass (m) × specific heat capacity (c). Since 'c' is the same and mass of A is twice that of B, the heat capacity of A is twice that of B.

questions.question: 5000 J of thermal energy is supplied to a 0.5 kg block of metal, raising its temperature by 20 °C. What is the specific heat capacity of the metal?
Why do coastal regions generally experience milder temperature variations between day and night compared to inland desert regions?
options: Water has a higher specific heat capacity than sand
Water has a lower specific heat capacity than sand
Sand absorbs more sunlight than water
Water reflects all thermal radiation at night
questions.explanation: Water has a much higher specific heat capacity than sand, meaning it requires more energy to heat up and releases more energy to cool down, moderating temperature changes.

questions.question: What happens to the thermal energy supplied to a substance during melting at its melting point?
options: It increases the kinetic energy of the particles, raising the temperature
It is used to overcome intermolecular forces, keeping the temperature constant
It is lost to the surroundings as latent heat of vaporization
It increases the potential energy of the nucleus of each atom
questions.explanation: During a phase change, the supplied thermal energy is used to break or weaken intermolecular bonds (increasing potential energy), not to increase kinetic energy, so the temperature remains constant.

questions.question: Calculate the thermal energy required to completely melt 0.2 kg of ice at 0 °C. [Specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 334,000 J/kg]
A burn from 100 °C steam is typically more severe than a burn from 100 °C boiling water. Why is this the case?
options: Steam has a higher specific heat capacity than water
Steam is at a higher temperature than boiling water
Steam releases a large amount of latent heat of vaporization when it condenses on the skin
Steam has a higher density than boiling water
questions.explanation: When steam condenses on the skin, it releases its specific latent heat of vaporization (a large amount of energy) in addition to the heat released as it cools down, causing more severe tissue damage.

questions.question: A straight vertical wire carries a current flowing downwards. What is the direction of the magnetic field lines around the wire when viewed from above?
questions.explanation: Using the Right-Hand Grip Rule: point the right thumb downwards (direction of current), and the fingers curl in a clockwise direction when viewed from above.

questions.question: Two parallel vertical wires carry currents in the same direction. What is the magnetic force between them?
options: There is no force between them
questions.explanation: Parallel currents in the same direction create magnetic fields that interact to produce an attractive force between the wires.

questions.question: Which of the following changes will NOT increase the strength of the magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid?
options: Increasing the current flowing through the wire
Increasing the number of turns per unit length
Inserting a soft iron core into the solenoid
Increasing the diameter of the solenoid coil while keeping the number of turns the same
questions.explanation: Increasing the diameter without adding more turns spreads the magnetic field lines further apart, which does not increase (and may slightly decrease) the magnetic field strength inside the core.

questions.question: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule, what does the middle (second) finger represent?
options: Direction of the force or motion
questions.explanation: In Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Thumb = Thrust (Force/Motion), First finger = Field (N to S), Second finger = Current (conventional, + to -).

questions.question: A horizontal wire carries a current from left to right. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field directed vertically downwards. What is the direction of the magnetic force on the wire?
questions.explanation: Using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: First finger points down (Field), second finger points right (Current). The thumb points out of the page (Force).

questions.question: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule is primarily used to determine the direction of:
options: The force on a current-carrying wire in a motor
The magnetic field around a straight wire
The induced current in a wire moving through a magnetic field
questions.explanation: Fleming's Right-Hand Rule (Thumb = Motion, First finger = Field, Second finger = Induced Current) is used for generators and electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: A copper wire is moved parallel to the magnetic field lines of a strong permanent magnet. What is the magnitude of the induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in the wire?
options: Depends on the speed of the wire
Depends on the length of the wire
questions.explanation: An e.m.f. is only induced when a conductor cuts across magnetic field lines. Moving parallel to the field lines means no field lines are cut, so the induced e.m.f. is zero.

questions.question: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 4 m. What is the speed of the wave?
questions.explanation: Using the wave equation v = fλ, v = 50 × 4 = 200 m/s.

questions.question: A water wave travels from deep water into shallow water. Which of the following correctly describes the changes in its properties?
options: Speed decreases, frequency decreases, wavelength decreases
Speed decreases, frequency remains constant, wavelength decreases
Speed increases, frequency remains constant, wavelength increases
Speed remains constant, frequency decreases, wavelength decreases
questions.explanation: When a wave changes medium, its frequency (determined by the source) remains constant. In shallow water, the speed decreases, which causes the wavelength to decrease (since v = fλ).

questions.question: The time period of a pendulum is 2.0 seconds. What is its frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency f = 1 / T = 1 / 2.0 = 0.5 Hz.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic unique to longitudinal waves and not found in transverse waves?
options: They consist of compressions and rarefactions
They can transfer energy through a vacuum
questions.explanation: Longitudinal waves (like sound) propagate via compressions and rarefactions parallel to the direction of energy transfer. Transverse waves have crests and troughs.

questions.question: A student measures the time for 20 complete oscillations of a wave to be 5.0 seconds. What is the frequency of the wave?
questions.explanation: Time period T = Total time / Number of oscillations = 5.0 / 20 = 0.25 s. Frequency f = 1 / T = 1 / 0.25 = 4.0 Hz.

questions.question: A sound wave travels through air at 340 m/s. If the distance between a compression and the adjacent rarefaction is 0.5 m, what is the frequency of the sound wave?
questions.explanation: The distance from a compression to the adjacent rarefaction is half a wavelength (λ/2). So, λ = 1.0 m. Using v = fλ, f = v / λ = 340 / 1.0 = 340 Hz.

questions.question: The magnetic field strength B at a distance d from a long straight wire is directly proportional to the current I and inversely proportional to d. If the current is doubled and the distance is halved, what happens to B?
questions.explanation: Since B ∝ I/d, the new field strength is proportional to (2I) / (0.5d) = 4(I/d). Therefore, the magnetic field strength quadruples.

questions.question: In an AC generator, at which position of the rotating coil is the induced e.m.f. momentarily zero?
options: When the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field lines
When the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field lines
When the coil is at a 45° angle to the magnetic field lines
The induced e.m.f. is never zero in an AC generator
questions.explanation: When the coil is perpendicular to the field, the magnetic flux is at a maximum, but the rate of change of flux is zero. Thus, the induced e.m.f. is momentarily zero.

questions.question: In an AC generator, the maximum induced e.m.f. is proportional to the number of turns (N) and the frequency of rotation (f). If N is doubled and f is halved, what happens to the maximum induced e.m.f.?
questions.explanation: Maximum e.m.f. ∝ N × f. If N becomes 2N and f becomes 0.5f, the product is (2N) × (0.5f) = Nf. The maximum induced e.m.f. remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of slip rings and carbon brushes in an AC generator?
options: To reverse the current direction every half rotation
To maintain continuous electrical contact with the rotating coil without twisting wires
To step up the output voltage using electromagnetic induction
To convert the alternating current into direct current
questions.explanation: Slip rings rotate with the coil while carbon brushes remain stationary, maintaining continuous electrical contact and allowing the naturally alternating current to be transferred to the external circuit.

questions.question: Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it, provided that:
options: The length of the conductor is doubled
The physical conditions, such as temperature, remain constant
The conductor is made of a semiconductor material
questions.explanation: Ohm's law strictly applies only when physical conditions (most notably temperature) are kept constant, ensuring the resistance of the conductor does not change.

questions.question: The I-V characteristic graph of a filament lamp curves and becomes less steep as the voltage increases. What does this indicate?
options: The resistance of the filament decreases as it gets hotter
The resistance of the filament increases as it gets hotter
The filament obeys Ohm's law perfectly at all voltages
The current is inversely proportional to the voltage
questions.explanation: As voltage and current increase, the filament heats up. The increased thermal vibration of the metal ions impedes electron flow, increasing the resistance and causing the graph to curve.

questions.question: A semiconductor diode is connected in reverse bias. Which statement best describes its electrical behavior?
options: It has very low resistance and allows a large current to flow
It has very high resistance and allows virtually no current to flow
It acts as a perfect conductor with zero resistance
It generates its own electromotive force
questions.explanation: In reverse bias, the depletion layer widens, creating a very high resistance that prevents current from flowing (except for a negligible leakage current).

questions.question: A diode is connected in series with a resistor and an AC power supply. What is the shape of the voltage waveform measured across the resistor?
questions.explanation: The diode only allows current to flow during the positive half-cycles of the AC supply, blocking the negative half-cycles. This results in a half-wave rectified output.

questions.question: A potential divider consists of a 4 Ω resistor and a 6 Ω resistor connected in series across a 10 V supply. What is the potential difference across the 6 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: Using the potential divider formula: V_out = V_in × (R_2 / (R_1 + R_2)) = 10 × (6 / (4 + 6)) = 10 × 0.6 = 6 V.

questions.question: In a potential divider, R_1 is a fixed resistor and R_2 is a thermistor. The output voltage is measured across R_2. What happens to the output voltage when the temperature increases?
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, the resistance of the thermistor (R_2) decreases. Therefore, it takes a smaller share of the total potential difference, causing the output voltage across it to decrease.

questions.question: An LDR and a fixed resistor form a potential divider, with the output voltage taken across the LDR. Why is the output voltage high in the dark?
options: The LDR's resistance is low in the dark, drawing more current
The LDR's resistance is high in the dark, taking a larger share of the potential difference
The fixed resistor's resistance drops to zero in the dark
The battery voltage automatically increases in the dark
questions.explanation: In the dark, the resistance of an LDR is very high. In a series circuit, the component with the higher resistance takes a proportionally larger share of the total supply voltage.

questions.question: If a load resistor is connected in parallel with the bottom resistor (R_2) of a potential divider, what happens to the output voltage across R_2?
options: It becomes equal to the input voltage
questions.explanation: Adding a resistor in parallel with R_2 decreases the combined resistance of the lower part of the divider. This lower resistance takes a smaller share of the total potential difference, reducing the output voltage.

questions.question: In a vacuum flask, the space between the double glass walls is evacuated. Which modes of heat transfer does this specifically prevent?
questions.explanation: Conduction and convection both require a material medium (particles) to transfer heat. A vacuum lacks particles, effectively preventing both conduction and convection.

questions.question: Why are the cooling pipes at the back of a refrigerator often painted black and designed with a large surface area?
options: To absorb more thermal radiation from the kitchen
To emit infrared radiation more effectively to the surroundings
To increase heat transfer by conduction to the wall
To prevent convection currents from forming
questions.explanation: Black, dull surfaces are the best emitters of infrared radiation. A large surface area further maximizes the rate of heat loss to the surrounding air.

questions.question: Why are metals generally much better conductors of heat than non-metals?
options: Metals have a higher specific heat capacity
Metals are denser, so particles are closer together
Metals contain free electrons that rapidly transfer kinetic energy through the lattice
Metals reflect thermal radiation better than non-metals
questions.explanation: In metals, delocalized free electrons gain kinetic energy when heated and move rapidly throughout the metal lattice, transferring thermal energy much faster than the vibration of ions alone.

questions.question: A shiny metal teapot keeps tea hot longer than a black ceramic teapot of the same mass and initial temperature. Why?
options: Shiny surfaces are poor emitters of infrared radiation
Shiny surfaces are good absorbers of infrared radiation
Metal has a higher specific heat capacity than ceramic
The metal teapot is heavier than the ceramic one
questions.explanation: Shiny, polished surfaces are poor emitters (and poor absorbers) of infrared radiation, significantly reducing the rate of heat loss via radiation compared to dull, black surfaces.

questions.question: A 12 V battery is connected to a potential divider with a 200 Ω resistor and a 400 Ω resistor in series. What is the potential difference across the 400 Ω resistor?
Double-glazed windows consist of two panes of glass with a narrow layer of air trapped between them. Why is this trapped air highly effective at reducing heat loss from a building?
options: Air is a good conductor of thermal energy
Air is a poor conductor, minimizing heat transfer by conduction
Air completely blocks all infrared radiation
Air prevents the glass from expanding
questions.explanation: Gases like air are very poor conductors of heat. Trapping the air in a narrow space also prevents convection currents from forming, making it an excellent thermal insulator.
